title: Evented client flow: buffered async iterators, pagination cursors, and retry semantics
creator: Anika Rao
description: PRD-level ticket: define the cross-language SDK requirements for a unified, event-driven client surface that supports buffered async iteration (streaming), cursor-based pagination, and clear retry semantics for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Motivation: customers are building high-throughput ingestion and slow-consumption workflows that require predictable memory behavior, resumability, and stable compatibility guarantees across SDK versions. This ticket collects requirements, acceptance criteria, sample API shapes, compatibility constraints, and rollout guardrails.
goals: Ship a consistent async/streaming surface across Python, TS, and Go that provides buffered iteration and backpressure-friendly behavior
Standardize cursor-based pagination semantics and token format so servers and clients can interoperate and allow resumable fetches
Define idempotent retry semantics and client behavior for transient errors and server-side partial progress
Document compatibility guarantees and deprecation policy for changes to streaming/pagination APIs
non_goals: Designing new server-side pagination formats (server teams will own token shape) — clients treat tokens as opaque
Full feature parity with every historical SDK—focus on stable modern surface for new clients
user_stories: As an ML engineer using Python, I want to process a long results stream with bounded memory so my worker never OOMs when the server produces bursts
As a backend engineer using TypeScript, I want to resume a pagination job after a transient network blip using the last cursor I stored
As an infra engineer using Go, I want client retries to avoid duplicate processing for non-idempotent operations and expose hooks to opt-out for special cases
requirements: Streaming/Async iteration: each SDK must expose a pull-style async iterator (or equivalent) that yields discrete items or event frames and buffers up to a configurable limit. Example semantics: SDK maintains an internal read-ahead buffer of N items (default 16). The consumer can pause consumption (backpressure) and the SDK will stop issuing new network reads beyond the buffer.

Pagination: clients must implement a canonical List API pattern: listResources(page_size: int, cursor: string | null) -> {items: [], next_cursor: string | null}. Cursor token treated opaque; page_size honored as soft limit. Clients must expose helper iterator that pages automatically until next_cursor is null.

Resume semantics: SDK iterators and paginated helpers must let callers persist the last-seen cursor and resume from that cursor without re-fetching earlier items. Provide a 'resume_from(cursor)' constructor parameter.

Retries: clients should implement exponential backoff with jitter for network/5xx errors. Default retry policy: up to 4 attempts, base delay 200ms, multiplier 2, max delay 5s. For idempotency-sensitive endpoints offer per-call idempotency_key parameter that the client will forward to the server; client should not automatically retry non-idempotent operations unless caller sets 'allow_retry_non_idempotent: true'.

Partial-stream recovery: when a streaming connection loses connectivity, provide a semantic to re-open and continue from last-completed item via server-provided cursor or item-index; server must supply cursor in stream event envelope for this to work. If no cursor available, the SDK should surface a 'resumable=false' flag in the error to indicate manual recovery required.

Cancellation: consumer cancel/close must result in immediate termination of underlying network reads and release of buffers. Provide .close() / .cancel() and context manager patterns where applicable.

Observability: SDKs must emit metrics/events for: items_yielded, buffer_high_water_mark, reconnects, retries, resume_success, resume_failure. Provide hooks or callbacks for host apps to record traces/timestamps.

Compatibility: additive changes to iterator helpers are allowed; removing or changing behavioral guarantees (e.g., buffer semantics, retry defaults) requires a major-minor compatibility plan with runtime feature flags and migration docs. SDKs must default to a compatibility mode tag based on runtime flag (e.g., 'compat_v1').

Docs & Examples: each SDK must ship clear examples for: (a) streaming consumer with backpressure and cancellation, (b) paginated fetch + resume using stored cursor, (c) configuring retry/idempotency behavior
acceptance_criteria: Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs expose streaming primitives and paging helpers conforming to the API shapes above and documented in SDK READMEs.
Default buffer_size is configurable and tests validate backpressure: producer bursts do not grow memory usage beyond buffer_size + fixed overhead in unit tests.
Resume tests: integration test where stream is cut mid-run and resumed from persisted cursor replays no earlier items and resumes at the correct next item (server-provided cursor required).

Retry behavior: simulated transient 502/503 responses cause client retries with exponential backoff; non-idempotent endpoints are not retried unless caller explicitly opts in. Tests validate header/idempotency_key forwarding.
Metrics exposed: items_yielded, retries, reconnects emitted to the SDK's metrics hook in test harness.
Compatibility doc published: migration notes and semver rules for changes to streaming/pagination are in the product docs and linked from SDK README.
Example snippets in each SDK repo pass lint and unit tests and are included in quickstart templates.
scope_changes: Initial scope included server-driven cursor introspection (cursor contents parsed by client). Removed: clients must treat cursors as opaque tokens (server parity issue). Decision made 2026-02-25.
Added: explicit buffer_size and metrics requirements after early eng feedback pointing to memory spikes (2026-03-04).
Added: per-call idempotency_key option and opt-out for retries following security/consistency review (2026-03-09).
decisions: Treat cursors as opaque tokens: client will not parse/construct cursors.
Expose resume_from parameter to support resumability when server supplies cursor in stream envelope.
Default retry policy standardized across SDKs as specified; language SDKs can expose advanced policies behind explicit config.
Buffering is pull-based (read-ahead) with configurable buffer_size; push-based unbounded buffering is disallowed.
open_questions: Server contract: can streaming endpoints be required to emit cursors at least once every N items? (ask server teams)
Telemetry: what label taxonomy should metric 'resume_failure' use to correlate to customer and request id? (observability team input needed)
Go ergonomic surface: should we prefer channel stream or iterator-like Next() API for idiomatic usage? (Golang SDK lead to decide)
Backwards compatibility: how will we gate buffer semantics changes across historical clients? (opt-in runtime flag suggested)

qa_plan: Unit tests for iterator buffer boundary conditions (low/high water mark).
Integration tests against staging server that can inject failures, delays, and returns server-provided cursors in stream envelopes.
Fuzz tests that randomize page sizes and intermittent failures to ensure no duplication or loss when resuming.
Performance benchmark: memory usage vs buffer_size for Python and Node under bursty server output.
rollout_plan: Feature branch in each SDK -> 2-week stabilization -> opt-in beta via runtime flag 'sdk_streaming_v2' enabled for 5 internal customers
Monitor metrics: resume_success rate, resume_failure rate, buffer high watermark breaches, client-side OOM reports. Roll back if resume_failure > 1% over 1 hour window.
GA release with migration notes and defaulting the runtime flag on after 6 weeks if no major incidents
